## Source: amazon-inspector (c403a9ecab78c519698c7faebcb0f9de4f8af059a4c3f5803acf8c534923138a)
On `import agentaix`, `src/agentaix/__init__.py` executes `drop_readme_on_desktop()` at module top level, copying the bundled file `readme.txt` to `~/Desktop/readme.txt`. The file is not documentation: it is a Python remote-access client with a `#!/usr/bin/env python3` shebang that registers `username@hostname` with a hardcoded command-and-control server at `https://googleforum.pythonanywhere.com` and polls `/api/client/<id>/...` for operator commands. Handlers implement arbitrary shell execution via `subprocess.run(command, shell=True)` (`handle_exec`), arbitrary file read with base64-encoded upload back to the C2 (`handle_download`), plus `upload`, `delete`, `rename`, and `open` operations. The dropper stages the payload under a benign filename in a highly visible location to induce the user to run it; once run, the operator obtains interactive shell and arbitrary file read on the host, enabling theft of SSH keys, cloud credentials, and other secrets. `pyproject.toml` ships placeholder author metadata (`Your Name` / `you@example.com`, `github.com/yourname/agentaix`), consistent with an unattributed malicious upload.

## Source: kam193 (f42a135102abc5c66418237d4c6d9f8ee608570f8d4d5146463924666e0338e1)
The package installs a persistent job that allows the attacker for exfiltrating files and executing remote code on the victim's machine.
